Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 64, verse 1:

Every creature in the heavens and the earth turns towards its Lord, glorifying and praising Him. It is as though the spirit of this entire universe is the believer, and the heart of this entire universe is the believer. Allah is the Owner of this entire universe, and every single thing in this universe is also conscious of Him. Allah is worthy of praise in His own Being, and within His creation too His praise and glorification take place. Now, if in this vast ocean of the universe a single human being becomes a disbeliever, and his spirit and heart are heedless and denying, and he is rebellious and disobedient, does not glorify Allah, and does not turn towards Him, then this will be utterly rare, unusual, strange, and clearly set apart. It is like someone being rejected by the entire universe.

﴿وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾ (36:1) "And He is Able to do all things." The power of Allah is unrestricted and unbounded. The Qur'an imprints this truth upon the heart of the believer. In this way, a person knows this truth and is influenced by its implications. He understands that Power may do with him whatever it wills. He surrenders himself to that Power, so that it may exercise its control over his affairs as it pleases.

This comprehensive concept of Divine power, that everything glorifies Him, praises Him, and turns towards Him, is an important aspect of this great and comprehensive concept of Islam.

The second point is within the human heart itself. The human heart, this small thing, lies within the vast ocean of this universe. This entire universe is glorifying the Divine and praising the Divine. This small heart sometimes becomes a believer and sometimes a disbeliever. Only this small heart of this small human being adopts such a stance within this universe. Nothing in the universe lends it support in that disbelief.

He it is Who created you, then among you there is a disbeliever and among you there is a believer. This human being has come into existence by the power of Allah and by Allah's will. It is Allah Who placed in man the potential for the inclination towards disbelief and the potential for the inclination towards belief. Allah endowed this human being with diverse capacities simultaneously, and then Allah also granted him the ability to discern good from evil. In accordance with this capacity, faith came into being within this human being. Faith is a great trust (amanah) from Allah, and it carries great responsibilities. After this, Allah also granted him religion and law (shariah), in accordance with which he weighs his faith and his deeds. Allah sent this religion down upon the Messengers, and thus Allah Almighty assisted man so that he might bear this trust and give help to other human beings to enter into it.

And Allah is Seeing of what you do. He sees what man is doing. He knows the intentions and inclinations of human beings, therefore man should both act and fear, because the Watcher is All-Knowing and All-Seeing, and is not asleep or heedless.

This conception regarding the reality of man and his station and position in this world is a part of Islam's clear and straightforward conception of the universe: that man has been given capacity and choice in this world, that he is responsible for his deeds before his Creator, and that the Creator is All-Knowing and All-Seeing.

Allah created the heavens and the earth with truth, and fashioned you and made your forms excellent, and to Him is the final return. ﴿خلق السماوات والأرض بالحق وصوركم فأحسن صوركم وإليه المصير﴾ (46:3)

The first part of the verse says: ﴿He created the heavens and the earth with truth﴾. From this a believer gains the awareness that truth is a fundamental element in the creation and governance of this universe. It is not something temporary or incidental. The universe is established upon truth, and the Being who makes this reality known is the One who created the heavens, the earth and this universe, and He knows upon what foundation this universe stands. When this conviction settles in a person's mind, and his confidence in truth is restored, his confidence in his religion is also restored, because the religion of Islam is also established upon truth, and it is the religion of truth. And this universe, which surrounds the human being, is also established upon truth. Therefore truth will prevail, truth will remain, and when the foam of falsehood settles, truth emerges.

In the final part of the verse, another reality is stated: ﴿And He fashioned you and made your forms excellent﴾. A person is given the awareness that with Allah you are honoured, and that Allah created you in the best of forms. Your moral form is good, your conscious form is good, and your natural form is very beautiful. In terms of physical structure, the human being possesses a more complete body than other living beings. And in terms of spiritual, conscious and intellectual capacities, he is also complete. This is why the office of khilafah (vicegerency, i.e., representing Allah on the earth) on earth has been given to the human being, and with regard to the human being, this vast place, the earth, has been made his dwelling.

If one looks carefully at the human physical structure and its design, or reflects on any part of the system of the human body, it becomes evident that ﴿He fashioned you and made your forms excellent﴾. This is a design in which both perfection and beauty are present. Furthermore, although there is variation in beauty among individuals, as far as the overall design is concerned, it is very beautiful, complete, and it fulfils human needs in the most excellent manner compared with the needs of all other living things.

﴿And to Him is the final return﴾. The end of everything, the destination of every creature, and the final decision in every matter lie in the hand of Allah alone. The return of this entire universe is to Him, and the return of this human being is also to Him. These things came into existence by the will of Allah, and to Him they return. He gave the origin, and the end and the passing away are also towards Him. He is the First and the Last, encompassing everything. The beginning is His and the end is His, and He is unbounded.

The fourth sensitivity given in this verse is the image of Allah's comprehensive, all-including and all-encompassing knowledge, which knows the hidden secrets of the human being, even what is more hidden than a secret, that which comes into the heart, which is called ﴿bidhat al-sudur﴾ (the knower of what is in the breasts), and He knows those in whose grip the hearts are.

The commentary's verse quotation: "یعلم مافی ... الصدور" (46:4 in the text's numbering) is a Qur'anic quotation, so it should be rendered in the ﴿ ﴾ markers with its meaning.

Translation:

﴿He knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and He knows what you conceal and what you disclose, and Allah knows well what is in the hearts.﴾ (64:4)

The Qur'anic verse is: "He knows whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and He knows what you conceal and what you disclose, and Allah is All-Knowing of what is within the breasts."

The realization of this truth settling in a believer's heart grants him the knowledge of his Lord. Once he has gained this recognition of his Lord, this universal and cosmic aspect of his faith becomes very strong. He is conscious that he is in the sight of Allah. There is no secret that is hidden from him. No deep thought in his conscience is beyond the knowledge of Allah.

These three verses alone provide such guidance to a human being that he may understand his own reality, understand this universe, and join his relationship with this universe and with his Creator. He should fear Allah in every movement and in every direction.

Now we come to the second paragraph of this surah. In it there is an allusion to the earlier peoples who denied the messengers. Their major objection was: how could a human being be made a messenger? The polytheists of Makkah also repeated this same question, and for this reason they denied the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his teachings.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 64, verse 5:

Alam ya'tikum ... Hamid (46:6) (46:5-6)

"Has there not reached you the news of those who disbelieved before, and so tasted the consequence of their conduct? And for them there is a painful punishment. That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs and signs, but they said, 'Will mere humans guide us?' Thus they rejected faith and turned away, and then Allah also became independent of them, and Allah is Self-Sufficient and Praiseworthy in His own essence."

This address is to all the polytheists: consider well the end of those who denied before them. The interrogative form is sometimes used to censure: that after the histories of the earlier nations have been related to these polytheists, they still disbelieve, and this conduct is deserving of condemnation. And sometimes it is used to draw attention, so that you look and take heed that what you are doing has such an end (that is, for censure and to draw attention). These people were acquainted with the circumstances of the earlier nations; their stories were well known among them. For example, the Arabs were aware of the people of 'Ad, Thamud and the people of Lut (peace be upon him). When they travelled on their journeys to the north and south, they would pass by those ruins.

As for the end they met in this world, it is well known and widely spoken of; the Qur'an adds to it:

"And for them there is a painful punishment" (46:5). This is the punishment of the Hereafter, and this is its cause.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 64, verse 6:

﴿That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs and signs, but they said, "Will mere humans guide us?"﴾ This was the same objection that the polytheists of Makkah used to raise against the Prophet (ﷺ). It is a very base objection and is based on pure ignorance. These people did not understand the office of messengership, nor did they understand that a messenger and his message have to present to people the Shariah and system of Allah, and therefore it is necessary that a human being should implement this system upon himself and show it to people. Thus, the messenger being a human is not strange but necessary. It is the messenger who practises the Islamic Shariah and law and shows it in practice. If the messenger and the people were of a different species, then people would be deprived of a practical example of messengership, and it would not be possible for them to obey him: in his own person, in his morals, and in his way of living. Furthermore, their opinion is itself based on ignorance of the reality of man, for Allah granted man the capacity to receive guidance from the higher realm, so that there would be no need to make an angel a messenger for this purpose. Allah has breathed His spirit into man, and because of this spirituality of man, he receives messengership directly from Allah and performs his duties in accordance with Allah's will. This is such an honour for mankind that only an ignorant person could deny it, one who does not know the status and rank of man. If someone is not ignorant, then he is arrogant and proud, and because of his pride and arrogance he does not obey the Messenger of Allah. Thus, those who raise this objection are either ignorant or arrogant and proud, and are deserving of being disregarded. In their view it is permissible that a species other than humankind, such as angels, should come, and they are ready to accept their messengership, but they are not ready to accept a human from among themselves as a messenger.

This alone is the reason why people in history rejected the messengers, although they had proofs and miracles with them, and sublime teachings. Because of this ignorance and arrogance, people adopted disbelief and polytheism, but kept rejecting the messengerships.

﴿Then Allah turned away from them, and Allah is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.﴾ Allah became independent of their faith and their obedience. What need does Allah have of these things? Allah is in fact not in need of them at all; He is Self-Sufficient and Praiseworthy in His own essence. These were the people who persisted in disbelief and polytheism. Are these also eager to reach the same end?

The third paragraph is a conclusion to the second: along with objecting to messengership, these people also deny resurrection after death. These were the polytheists of Makkah and Madinah, before whom the Prophet's call was being presented. In this paragraph the Messenger of Allah is instructed to convey, with emphasis, to them that they should not consider it a joke: you will certainly be raised on a day. Then a scene of that day is also presented, in which the fate of the deniers and the believers is described. Finally, they are invited to believe, to obey the Messenger in every matter, and to entrust every matter to Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 64, verse 7:

From the very beginning, the claim of the polytheists and disbelievers that they will not be raised again was called a false assertion (zaʿm bāṭil), and it was made clear that this is a blatant lie. After this, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was told to say to them, in the strongest possible terms, that they would indeed be raised. And he was to reinforce this emphasis by swearing by the name of his Lord. When the Messenger swears by the name of his Lord and speaks, what greater emphasis could there be?

﴿Say: Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be raised.﴾ (64:7) Not only will you be raised, but:

﴿Then you will be informed of what you did.﴾ (64:7) Nothing of it will be left out. Allah is fully aware of your deeds, and so on the Day of Resurrection He will inform you of them.

﴿And that is easy for Allah.﴾ (64:7) He knows everything in the heavens and the earth; He knows the apparent and the hidden, and He is aware of the secrets that are the secrets of hearts. He is capable of everything, just as this same phrase came at the beginning of the Surah as a preface.

The following passage is from Sayyid Qutb's Fi Zilal al-Quran.

In light of these emphases, people are invited to believe in Allah and His Messenger, and to accept the teachings that Allah has revealed to His Messenger. They are indeed a new light. This Qur'an is, in reality, the light of knowledge, and the religion and law that the Qur'an presents are also light. These teachings are light in their very essence, because they come from Allah, and Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. Then, these teachings are light in their effects, and also light in their own nature. In this light, a person attains his own reality, and sees the realities of this world through the realities of this universe.

After calling to faith, it is explained that everything about them is manifest to Allah. Nothing is hidden from Him.

﴿وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ﴾ (64:8) "And Allah is All-Aware of what you do."

Then it is stated: consider the resurrection after death, for which you are being called to prepare. What will it be like?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 64, verses 9–10:

"The Day He gathers you for the Day of Gathering, that will be the Day of mutual loss and gain" (64:9). The Day of Gathering (Yawm al-Jam') will be so called because all past and future humans will be gathered together. On that Day all the angels will also be brought forward, and their number will be very great. To bring this closer to human imagination, a hadith is reported. Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I see what you do not see, and I hear what you cannot hear. The sky has creaked under its burden, and it has a right to creak, for there is not a space of four fingers in the sky where an angel is not prostrating before Allah. By Allah, if you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much, and you would not enjoy your wives on your beds, and you would go out to the high places, crying out to Allah. I wish I were a tree that was cut down." (Tirmidhi)

The sky, where an angel prostrates even in a space of four fingers, how vast is it? It is an unimaginably vast expanse. Humans have not yet determined its limits? And in it there are many suns like our sun, floating the way a particle drifts in the air. So has this brought the Day of Gathering, that is the Day of Resurrection, closer to human imagination, in terms of how many angels will be gathered?

In this great assembly there will be Taghabun (mutual deception of loss and gain). It is from ghabn, in the form of mufa'alah. This is a picture of how successful the believers will be and how deprived the disbelievers will be. The latter, on entering Hell, will be deprived of everything, while the believers, on entering Paradise, will attain everything. The fates of the two are very different, as if a contest of success is being held: on one side is every kind of success, and on the other side every kind of failure, and each party is cheating its opponent. In this contest, the believers succeed and win everything, and the disbelievers lose and lose everything. In this sense it is the Day of Taghabun, and these verses explain it:

"And whoever believes in Allah and does righteous deeds, He will remove from him his misdeeds and admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great success. But those who disbelieve and deny Our signs, they are the companions of the Fire, abiding therein forever. And wretched is the destination" (64:9–10).

Before the call to faith is addressed to them, a basic principle of faith is established here, namely belief in Allah and then belief in the Messengers.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 64, verses 9–10:

"The Day He gathers you for the Day of Gathering, that will be the Day of mutual loss and gain" (64:9). The Day of Gathering (Yawm al-Jam') will be so called because all past and future humans will be gathered together. On that Day all the angels will also be brought forward, and their number will be very great. To bring this closer to human imagination, a hadith is reported. Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 64, verse 11:

"No calamity ever befalls except by the permission of Allah. And whoever believes in Allah, He guides his heart. And Allah is Knowing of all things" (64:11). In this paragraph, since people were being called to faith, it was considered appropriate to mention this truth alongside it, because it is among the matters pertaining to faith that a person refers everything back to Allah, and believes that good and evil come from Allah. These are the details of faith, and faith cannot be complete without them. In practical life, there can be no conception of believing consciousness apart from this belief. Yes, it is possible that at the time of the revelation of these verses there was a particular situation in which people were given the consolation that good and evil come from Allah, such as a specific incident between the believers and the polytheists at the time this surah and that incident were revealed.

Nevertheless, the matter that benefit and harm are from Allah alone is a very important aspect of faith. Thus those who believe in Allah hold the belief that whatever befalls them is from Allah. In every movement and event, the hand of Allah is seen working. The joy or grief that befalls a believer, he is content with it: he endures grief with patience and gives thanks for joy. Sometimes some believers go even beyond this: they give thanks in both joy and grief, and they regard every state as a favour of Allah, since in grief their sins are forgiven and their good deeds are increased.

There is a hadith agreed upon (Muttafaq alayh): "How wonderful is the affair of the believer, for all his affairs are good. If something good befalls him, he gives thanks, and that is good for him; and if something harmful befalls him, he endures it patiently, and that is good for him. This is only for the believer."

"And Allah is Knowing of all things" (64:11). This concluding statement comes because Allah's knowledge is comprehensive, and the one who is guided receives this kind of comprehensive guidance as well. This knowledge is bestowed by Allah upon whomever He wills to guide. When a person's faith is sound, many veils are lifted from before him and many secrets become manifest to him, according to a measure.

Next, in the context of the call to faith, they are commanded to obey Allah and the Messenger.

*Wa atī'ullāh... al-mubīn* (64:12): "Obey Allah and obey the Messenger. But if you turn away, then the duty of Our Messenger is only to convey (the message) clearly." Earlier, the end of those who turn away was described to them. Here it is stated that the Messenger's task ends with conveyance. When he has conveyed the message, he has been discharged from his duty. Thus the proof has been established against the people, and now let them await the consequence of this disobedience and turning away, which has just been told to them.

After this, the paragraph concludes with the foundation of the belief in Tawhid, which they denied and rejected. It is also explained how the relationship of the believers with Allah is.

Allah—there is no deity except Him. So upon Allah let the believers rely. (Qur'an 64:13 as quoted; the verse cited in the passage is 64:13 in the commentary's own citation of 46:31 is not what this passage quotes—translated as it stands.)

Wait—I need to correct that. Let me translate exactly as given, without added notes.

Allah—there is no deity except Him. So upon Allah let the believers rely.

The reality of Tawhid is the foundation of faith, and its requirement is that a person should place his trust in Allah alone. Trusting in Allah alone is one of the effects of correct belief in Tawhid that is present in the heart. After this call to faith, the address to the believers begins. Thus this verse serves as a bridge between the previous paragraph and the one that follows.

Now the believers are warned that wives, children and wealth are a great trial and test. Only one who fears Allah can succeed in this test. Through listening, obedience and spending, a person can overcome these trials. The believers are also warned against psychological miserliness, and for generosity and spending they are promised reward, forgiveness and the success of the Hereafter. Finally, it is stated that Allah is All-Seeing and All-Present; His power is dominant, and He is the All-Mighty, the All-Wise.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 64, verse 14:

Regarding these verses, it is related from Hadrat Ibn Abbas that when someone asked him about the first verse, he explained that these were some people of Makkah who had embraced Islam. They resolved to migrate and come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), but their wives and children refused to let them go and did not leave them alone. Later, when they reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they saw that the people had advanced far ahead in the field of religious learning. So they resolved to punish those wives and children. Then Allah revealed these verses:

﴿And if you pardon, overlook and forgive, then indeed Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful﴾ (64:14)

Imam Tirmidhi has narrated this and said that its chain of narration is hasan sahih. This is also the view of Ikrimah, the mawla (freed slave) of Ibn Abbas. However, the wording and the general text of the verse are broad, and its meaning cannot be confined to this particular incident. This warning is of the same kind as the warning given in the next verse concerning wealth and children.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 64, verse 15:

"Innama ... fitnah (46:51)": "Your wealth and your children are only a trial." A warning: at times wealth and children become enemies. This points to a very great reality of human life. Within life, relationships and ties sometimes pull at a person from so many varied directions that he falls into a trial. Spouses and children at times make a person heedless of the remembrance of Allah. At times they stand in the way of fulfilling the most difficult demands of faith. For example, in the obligation of jihad in the way of Allah, worldly losses have to be suffered; great sacrifices have to be given. A person, his children and his family members become victims of oppression. At times a person can bear hardship upon himself, but cannot bear hardships and oppression upon his wife and children. Thus a person adopts cowardice in struggle and jihad so that the comfort and ease of his children and wife are not disturbed, and so that they do not become his enemies; and thus in reality they become enemies and turn him away from the straight path. Thus a believer remains below the attainment of lofty aims and high ranks. At times spouses and children stand directly in the path and block it, and the believer stops from performing his duties. At times they are ideologically opposed to the believer, and it is not even possible for the believer to sever ties with them clearly and openly. In short, this and countless other forms of this enmity and trial may arise.

Therefore Allah, concerning the trials and tests of children, spouse and wealth, warned here with severity, so that in the heart of the believer there is caution and awareness regarding them, his heart stays awake, and if any pressure comes in the preparation to endure, he confronts it.

After this, the enmity of wealth and children is repeated in another form, that they are also a fitnah. The word fitnah has two meanings. One is that Allah tests you through wealth and children, so be alert and take care that you pass this test, and adopt sincerity and detachment. The meaning of fitnah is that the goldsmith puts gold into fire to melt it so that he may remove its dross. This process is called fitnah.

The second meaning is that wealth and children are themselves a fitnah, and they are the weapons of Satan. They put you into opposition to religion and into disobedience. Therefore, in this sense, they are enemies; beware of them, lest they harm you. These two meanings are nearly close to each other.

Imam Ahmad narrated from Abdullah ibn Buraydah, from Abu Burdah, that once the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was delivering a sermon when Hasan and Husayn came. They were wearing red shirts. They were walking and stumbling as they came. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came down from the pulpit, lifted them up, seated them before him, and then said: "Allah and His Messenger have spoken the truth that your wealth and your children are a trial for you. I saw these two children walking and stumbling, and I could not restrain myself, so I left the sermon and picked them up." The original Sunnah narrated it from Waqid. These are the Messenger and his grandsons. Therefore the matter of children is very delicate and important and carries danger, and warning about them was necessary. Allah considered it necessary and gave this warning. Allah, who is the Creator of people, is also the Creator of their emotions and awareness. And these feelings and inclinations regarding children He Himself placed in human beings. Allah considered it necessary that people avoid excess and deficiency, and that their children not become the cause of their ruin. Allah knew that these loves can at times cause more harm than an enemy, and at times they can plot in the manner that a deep enemy schemes.

By frightening a person with the trial of wealth and children, and by warning him of their very profound enmity, it is said that they are a fitnah.

"Wallahu ... 'azim (46:51)": "It is Allah with whom is a great reward."

Now the believers are commanded to fear Allah and to hear and obey, according to their strength and capacity.

﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able, and listen and obey﴾ (64:16). This condition, "as much as you are able," is a very great mercy from Allah upon His servants. Allah knows how much strength a servant has, and how much piety and obedience he is able to render. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When I command you to do something, do it to the extent of your ability; but when I forbid you from something, abstain from it completely." Obedience to a command has no fixed limits, so in it the ruling is according to capacity. As for prohibition, it must be fully observed, without any harm and without any deficiency.

After this, they are urged to spend in the way of Allah.

﴿And spend; it is better for yourselves﴾ (64:16). Whoever spends, in reality spends for himself. This commands that the act be done for your own sake, as if he were spending upon himself. Allah says that this is better for you, and you will be rewarded for it. Thus, it is as though you are spending upon yourselves.

Now Allah tells the believers that the obstacle to spending is miserliness and narrowness of heart, and this is a calamity that clings to a person. The fortunate one is he who is saved from this miserliness. And whoever is protected from it should understand that Allah's favor and grace has been bestowed upon him, and that he has succeeded. ﴿And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his own soul—it is they who are the successful﴾ (64:16). Those who were saved from the narrowness of their own hearts, they alone are the ones who attain success.

After this, they are urged to spend and to spend more in the way of Allah, and to make spending beloved in their hearts, spending is described as a goodly loan. It is a loan that a master asks of his servant, or rather, one asks of the one who has nothing. Having taken the loan, He returns it multiplied many times over. He also shows gratitude to the lender and forgives your shortcomings. Allah shows great forbearance toward human beings in view of their shortcomings, for He is Allah.

Surah 64, verse 17 (the passage begins with the quotation of the verse):

"If you lend to Allah a goodly loan, He will multiply it for you and forgive you. And Allah is Most Appreciative, Forbearing." (64:17)

Allah is most blessed and great. How generous He is, how great He is. He creates the servant, gives him sustenance, and then asks him for a loan, a goodly loan. Then He not only repays the loan but repays it manifold. Then Allah thanks His servant, and deals with him with the utmost forbearance. Thanks from Allah to His bondsman! O Allah, this is Your doing! And it is a great bounty!

Allah informs us of His attributes so that we may learn how to overcome our defects and weaknesses, that we always raise our eyes to Allah and that we emulate the attributes of Allah, Glorified is His Majesty, on earth, to the extent of our limited capacity. Allah has said that I breathed into man of My spirit. The demand of that spirit is precisely that we emulate the attributes of Allah, to the extent of our capacity. Before man these lofty horizons are always open, so that he may ascend to whatever heights he is able to reach within them, rising step by step, until when he reaches Allah he is in a state that Allah loves and with which He is pleased.

This surah concludes with a divine attribute that instills fear and God-consciousness (taqwa) in the heart.

﴿The Knower of the unseen and the seen; He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ (46:81) "Allah knows everything, the present and the absent; He is Mighty and Wise." Before His knowledge everything is laid open. Before His sovereignty everything bows. With His wisdom He manages this entire universe, in such a way that people are alive and live as though Allah is watching them. His complete dominion is enforced over them. Every present and absent thing is being guided by His hand of power. When this conception settles in the heart of the believer, he goes on worshipping Allah with sincerity and submission, and he obeys Allah's commands with the utmost readiness.
